inputs.original_text: Micheál Martin was in Limerick this past week trying to spin that housing tenancies have gone up, but that distracts from the surge in eviction notices and homelessness that came after the government's March 1 rules forcing landlords to offer six-year leases. Nationally the number of people stuck in emergency accommodation has increased again, exposing how these weak measures fail to protect vulnerable groups from the structural inequalities and landlord power driving the housing crisis. We need urgent, serious reforms to confront the root causes of exploitation and guarantee stable homes as a basic right instead of letting profits dominate—it's time to stop the system from serving the powerful at everyone else's expense.
inputs.modified_text: Micheál Martin was in Limerick this past week pushing the line that housing tenancies are up, but that line is just a distraction from the real surge in eviction notices and homelessness that followed the government's March 1 rules forcing landlords to offer six-year leases. Nationally the number of people stuck in emergency accommodation has increased again, and it shows how these weak measures do nothing to shield vulnerable groups from the structural inequalities and landlord power that drive the housing crisis. We need urgent, serious reforms to take on the root causes of exploitation and secure stable homes as a basic right instead of letting profits come first—it's long past time to dismantle a system built to serve the powerful at everyone else's expense.
